docs.title: Xp-clean
docs.text:
Xp-clean discovers and cleans up Crossplane v2 composition trees — test GVKs and leftover instances left behind in shared clusters.

It targets v2-native stacks only (Namespaced and modern Cluster XRs). LegacyCluster claims are not supported: there is no claim discovery or deletion path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Discover CompositeResourceDefinitions and select highest-parent XRs (roots mode). Full parent→child traces are opt-in (--mode=trace).
  2. Select eligible stacks with labels (day-1) and/or glob patterns (advanced). Namespace alone never implies eligibility.
  3. Plan with xp-clean run --once — dry-run by default (deletion.mode: roots, deletion.scope: instances-only).
  4. Execute only with --apply and policy dryRun: false (foreground Delete; --wait opt-in); skip paused resources; never strip Crossplane finalizers.
  5. Notify (optional, advanced) via Microsoft Teams Workflows on run start / finish / failure.

docs.text:

  • Versions — published with mike. Use the version selector in the header.
Version / alias Meaning latest Docs for the newest non-prerelease SemVer tag (default after the first release) 0.x.y Immutable docs for that release tag dev Docs from the tip of main (may change between releases)

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: Standalone Cobra binary xp-clean. kubectl plugin documentation is deferred — use the standalone CLI for now.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
xp-clean run --once [--config PATH] [--policy-namespace NS] [--apply] [--mode roots|trace] [--wait] [--dry-run=true|false] [--scope instances-only|all] [--gvk-glob G/V]… [--fail-on-blocked] [--notify] [--notify-on-dry-run] [--kubeconfig PATH] [--context NAME]
xp-clean plan [--config PATH] [--policy-namespace NS] [--mode …] [--scope …] [--gvk-glob G/V]… [--fail-on-blocked] [-o json|yaml]
xp-clean debug trace --name ns/name|--name name -n ns --group G --kind K [--version V] [-o text|json|yaml]
xp-clean manager [--config PATH] [--policy-namespace NS] [--apply] [--mode roots|trace] [--wait] [--gvk-glob G/V]…
xp-clean skill install [--project] [--force] [-a cursor]
xp-clean version [-o short|json|yaml]
xp-clean completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell
Command Role run --once Day-to-day. Discover → plan → optional execute. Defaults to a dry-run plan of roots (highest-parent stacks matched / would delete) plan Deprecated thin wrapper: machine-readable DeletePlans (-o json\|yaml), always dry-run debug trace Print one composition tree (debug only; -n valid here) manager Long-running schedule stub (same --apply / dry-run / mode / wait gates as run) skill install Install the embedded Cursor skill (~/.cursor/skills/xp-clean/ by default; --project for repo-local) version / completion Build metadata and shell completion

Root xp-clean trace remains as a hidden compatibility alias of debug trace.

docs.title: Flags worth knowing
docs.text:
Flag / env Notes --config / XP_CLEAN_CONFIG Required for file override — no implicit sample path --policy-namespace / XP_CLEAN_POLICY_NAMESPACE Namespace for labelled ConfigMaps (default xp-clean) --apply Happy-path live switch. Still requires policy dryRun: false. Without --apply, run always plans only --mode / XP_CLEAN_MODE roots (default) or trace. Roots-only plans highest-parent XRs; trace builds full parent→child trees --wait / XP_CLEAN_WAIT Opt-in: poll until each delete is gone (honours deletion.waitTimeout). Default is no wait --dry-run / XP_CLEAN_DRY_RUN Compatibility boolean planner dry-run (not kubectl API-server dry-run). --dry-run=true forces a plan; --dry-run=false allows live only when policy dryRun is false (prefer --apply) --scope / XP_CLEAN_SCOPE instances-only (default) or all --gvk-glob Repeatable group/version glob (same dialect as selectors.globs.gvks). When set, replaces policy GVK globs entirely (no merge). When omitted, policy globs (including none) are unchanged. Labels / TTL / other globs stay from policy --fail-on-blocked Exit 3 when the run completed with blocked plans --notify / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY Override notifications.enabled --notify-on-dry-run / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY_ON_DRY_RUN Override notifications.onDryRun -n / --namespace Valid on debug trace only. Rejected on run / plan (usage / exit 2) -v / --v Opt-in log verbosity: 0 error-only (default), 1 info, 2+ debug --log-level Zap level on stderr (debug\|info\|warn\|error); default error for interactive CLI. Alias: --zap-log-level

Logging stays on zap/logr end-to-end, but interactive commands (run, plan, debug trace, version) are quiet by default: only command results on stdout and real failures on stderr. Pass -v=1 (or --log-level=info) to restore detail. manager defaults to info. Client-go / discovery warning noise is muted unless verbose. Encoder flags: --zap-devel, --zap-encoder.

docs.title: run output
docs.text:
Default run --once (roots + instances-only) prints a compact human summary on stdout:

policy=<name> dryRun=<bool> mode=roots scope=instances-only
would delete N
  <Kind> <namespace>/<name> — <reason>
  …

Each object line includes the planner delete reason: mode tag plus eligibility cause (for example instance_root; label:xp-clean.io/eligible=true+ttl_elapsed). The same Kind namespace/name — reason shape is used on Teams Adaptive Cards and in audit JSON reason fields.

No per-object audit JSON, no trace … dumps, and no stack … steps=1 / numbered delete lines for single-step root plans. Restore richer plan detail and stdout audit JSON with -v=1 (or --log-level=info). Quiet summary (eligibility reasons included) is the default without -v. mode=trace, scope=all, and multi-step plans keep detailed stack listings without requiring -v. Machine-readable DeletePlans remain on plan -o json|yaml. Scheduled manager runs still emit audit JSON on stdout.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Runtime failure 2 Usage / validation (including -n on run/plan) 3 Blocked plans with --fail-on-blocked

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Flags > env > policy document > built-in defaults. No Viper. Webhook URLs come only from env vars named by each sink (default XP_CLEAN_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL).

Live deletes are two-key: CLI --apply (or compatibility --dry-run=false) and policy dryRun: false. Flags never unilaterally force live past a policy that still has dryRun: true.

Live deletes always use Kubernetes DeletionPropagation=Foreground. Waiting for the object to disappear is separate and off by default.

docs.title: Migration notes
docs.text: Old habit Prefer now xp-clean plan for interactive dry-run xp-clean run --once xp-clean plan -o json in scripts Still works (deprecated wrapper); or parse run summary / audit xp-clean trace … xp-clean debug trace … --dry-run=false for live --apply (and keep policy dryRun: false) Always walk full composition trees Default roots; opt in with --mode=trace / deletion.mode: trace Always poll after delete Opt in with --wait / deletion.wait: true

docs.title: Install and releases
docs.text: Tagged SemVer releases (v*) publish release artefacts. There is no snapshot publish from main.

docs.title: Artefacts
docs.text:
1. GitHub Release archives — linux and darwin (amd64 / arm64) plus checksums.txt (and archive SBOMs when Syft is available on the runner).
  2. GHCR image — ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean (linux amd64 / arm64).
Image tag Meaning :vX.Y.Z / :vX.Y.Z-rc.N Immutable pin (prefer this in clusters; RCs publish only this tag) :X.Y / :X Floating minor / major — moved only on non-prerelease cuts :latest Moved only on non-prerelease releases (RCs such as v0.2.0-rc.1 do not move it)

Visibility (locked): ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean is public and allows anonymous pulls. Release archives on GitHub are public with the repository. This matches the project preference (2026-11-01): keep the package public; do not delete or republish as private.

docs.title: CLI on your machine
docs.text:
Install the latest non-prerelease binary into ~/.local/bin (created if missing; the script never runs sudo for you):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanzifucius/xp-clean/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

Until the first non-prerelease cut, pin the current pre-release explicitly (for example v0.1.0-rc.1):

XP_CLEAN_VERSION=v0.1.0-rc.1 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanzifucius/xp-clean/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

docs.title: Pin a version
docs.text:
XP_CLEAN_VERSION=v0.1.0 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanzifucius/xp-clean/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
# or:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanzifucius/xp-clean/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.1.0

Use XP_CLEAN_VERSION (or --version) for any tag — including RCs such as v0.1.0-rc.1. Omit it only when you want the latest non-prerelease.

docs.title: Download, inspect, then run
docs.text:
Piping to bash is a convenience for trusted environments. For a cautious path:

curl -fsSL -o install.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanzifucius/xp-clean/main/scripts/install.sh
less install.sh
bash install.sh

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Mechanism Purpose XP_CLEAN_VERSION / --version Pin tag (v0.1.0, v0.1.0-rc.1, …); omit for latest non-prerelease XP_CLEAN_INSTALL_DIR / --install-dir / BINDIR Override install directory (default ~/.local/bin) GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN Optional — API rate limits, GHES, or a private fork

The installer downloads the platform archive and checksums.txt from the same release, verifies SHA-256 strictly, and installs only the xp-clean binary.

Supported platforms match GoReleaser archives: Linux/Darwin × x86_64 / arm64.

docs.title: PATH
docs.text:
If ~/.local/bin is not on your PATH, the script prints a hint. Add it yourself (the installer does not rewrite shell rc files):

export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

docs.title: Cursor skill
docs.text:
After the binary is on your PATH, install the embedded Cursor skill (teaches dry-run first, confirm before --apply, skinny eligibility, and --gvk-glob):

xp-clean skill install            # ~/.cursor/skills/xp-clean/SKILL.md
xp-clean skill install --project  # .cursor/skills/xp-clean/SKILL.md (git root / cwd)
xp-clean skill install --force    # overwrite

v1 supports Cursor only (-a/--agent cursor).

docs.title: CI tip
docs.text: For reproducible pipelines, prefer a pinned tag or gh release download of a specific archive over an unpinned pipe-to-bash.

docs.title: Manual download
docs.text: Browse GitHub Releases, download the matching xp-clean_<version>_<Os>_<Arch>.tar.gz and checksums.txt, verify the checksum, extract, and place xp-clean on your PATH.

docs.title: Run in-cluster (GHCR)
docs.text:
Package page: ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean.

Pull without registry login:

docker pull ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean:v0.1.0-rc.1

In-cluster Deployments / CronJobs can omit imagePullSecrets for this image.

If you consume a private fork of the package, authenticate and use an imagePullSecret whose token can read:packages:

# PAT or fine-grained token with read:packages (SSO-authorise if the org requires it)
echo "$CR_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u USERNAME --password-stdin
docker pull ghcr.io/NAMESPACE/xp-clean:v0.1.0

Use the same SemVer tag for the CLI archive and the image (for example v0.1.0) so operators can correlate laptop and cluster versions.

docs.title: Helm chart (in-cluster CronJob)
docs.text:
The chart installs into the dedicated xp-clean namespace:

  • Namespace, ServiceAccount
  • ClusterRole / ClusterRoleBinding (lab-oriented broad rules from the RBAC sketch; no claim RBAC)
  • Role / RoleBinding for reading policy ConfigMaps in xp-clean
  • Sample labelled policy ConfigMap (xp-clean.io/policy=true)
  • CronJob running xp-clean run --once (default install path)
  • Optional manager Deployment (manager.enabled, off by default — interval stub only)

There is no CleanupPolicy CRD in this chart. ConfigMaps remain the primary in-cluster policy surface.

docs.title: Install from GHCR (OCI)
docs.text:
On each SemVer git tag the release workflow packages the chart and pushes it to GHCR. Chart OCI tags are SemVer without a leading v; the default image.tag inside the package keeps v so it matches the published app image.

helm upgrade --install xp-clean oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean \
  --version 0.1.0-rc.1 \
  --namespace xp-clean \
  --create-namespace

helm show chart oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean --version 0.1.0-rc.1
helm template xp-clean oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean \
  --version 0.1.0-rc.1 --namespace xp-clean

The chart package (ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean) and the app image package are both public — no helm registry login or imagePullSecret for the happy path. After the first chart push, confirm the new GHCR package is set Public in GitHub Packages (same operational step as the image).

docs.title: Install from a repository checkout
docs.text:
helm upgrade --install xp-clean ./deploy/helm/xp-clean \
  --namespace xp-clean \
  --create-namespace \
  --set image.tag=v0.1.0-rc.1

For a private fork image, create a docker-registry secret and pass imagePullSecrets (and set image.repository as needed). Source chart path: deploy/helm/xp-clean.

docs.title: Important values
docs.text:
Value Default Purpose image.tag v0.1.0-rc.1 Pin the GHCR image (prefer immutable :vX.Y.Z) imagePullSecrets [] Optional; needed only for private fork pulls dryRun true When false, CronJob / manager get --apply cronjob.schedule 0 */6 * * * Kubernetes CronJob schedule cronjob.enabled true Default ops path manager.enabled false Optional secondary Deployment resources small requests/limits Pod resource settings policy.create true Install the sample policy ConfigMap

Live deletes need chart dryRun: false (passes --apply) and policy ConfigMap dryRun: false. Edit label selectors on the sample policy before enabling deletes. Full reference: the chart README.md and values.yaml.

docs.title: Maintainer: GHCR visibility
docs.text:
Locked decision (2026-11-01): keep ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean public (anonymous pull). Do not delete the package or republish it as private.

Package page: ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean. GitHub’s Container registry does not allow switching an already-public package back to private in Package settings (docs); that constraint is moot under the locked public preference.

docs.title: Cut a release (maintainers)
docs.text:
1. Ensure main is green.
  2. Tag and push (do not create the Release in the UI):
git checkout main && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "v0.1.0"
git push origin v0.1.0
  1. Watch the release workflow; confirm GitHub Release assets, docker pull ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean:v0.1.0, and helm show chart oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean --version 0.1.0.
  2. Spot-check xp-clean version -o json from the archive or image.
  3. On the first chart publish, set the GHCR package charts/xp-clean to Public (and link it to the repo) if GitHub created it private.

The docs workflow also deploys a versioned site for that tag (see Home for latest / dev aliases).

Release notes and assets: GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Build a local binary, point at a sample policy with an explicit --config, and run a dry-run plan against a cluster that can list XRDs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go matching go.mod (see repository root)
  • A kubeconfig that can list XRDs and the XR GVKs your selectors match

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
make test
make build   # writes bin/xp-clean with version ldflags

docs.title: Dry-run locally (file override)
docs.text:
There is no implicit sample path. Pass --config every time you use a file. run --once defaults to a dry-run plan (stacks matched / would delete):

go run ./cmd/xp-clean run --once \
  --config config/samples/cleanuppolicy.yaml \
  --kubeconfig "$HOME/.kube/config"

Scripts that need machine-readable DeletePlans can still use the thin deprecated wrapper:

go run ./cmd/xp-clean plan --config config/samples/cleanuppolicy.yaml -o json

Inspect one composition tree (debug only):

go run ./cmd/xp-clean debug trace \
  --name test-db -n xp-test-1 \
  --group db.dev.example.org \
  --kind XDB

Live deletes

Live deletes require --apply and policy dryRun: false. Deletes use foreground propagation. Waiting is opt-in (--wait). Prefer the default dry-run roots plan until stacks matched / would delete looks correct. Use --mode=trace for full trees. Xp-clean never strips Crossplane finalizers.

docs.title: In-cluster (Helm)
docs.text:
Prefer the published OCI chart (chart --version omits the leading v):

helm upgrade --install xp-clean oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean \
  --version 0.1.0-rc.1 \
  --namespace xp-clean \
  --create-namespace

From a checkout use deploy/helm/xp-clean and pin --set image.tag=v0.1.0-rc.1. That installs Namespace, ServiceAccount, RBAC, a sample policy ConfigMap (label eligibility + TTL + dry-run + instances-only), and a CronJob (xp-clean run --once) with dry-run on by default. The optional manager Deployment stays off unless manager.enabled=true.

Without Helm, apply config/rbac/role.yaml plus labelled ConfigMaps (xp-clean.io/policy=true, data key policy.yaml) from config/samples/.

See Policy and eligibility and Install for values, GHCR pull, and release notes.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Xp-clean is a Go CLI (and future in-cluster controller) for scheduled discovery and cleanup of Crossplane v2-native composition trees.

docs.title: MVP implemented in this repository
docs.text:
• Dynamic XRD discovery + instance trace build (no claims)
  • Eligibility via labels and/or globs + TTL (pkg/match); GVK globs are group/version
  • deletion.scope with default instances-only
  • Boolean dry-run planner by default; live deletes via --apply + policy dryRun: false; skip paused by default
  • Cleanup mode roots (default) or opt-in trace; in roots mode only XRs with no XR controller-owner are planned (parent need not match selectors); foreground Delete propagation; wait after delete opt-in
  • File / labelled ConfigMap policy (multi-tenant); explicit --config for file override
  • Cobra CLI: run (day-to-day) / deprecated plan / debug trace / manager / version / completion
  • Layout: thin cmd/xp-clean, internal/cli helpers, domain in pkg/
  • Optional Teams Workflows notification hooks around RunOnce
  • GoReleaser + public GHCR on SemVer tags (anonymous pull; see Install); CI with golangci-lint
  • Minimal Helm chart (deploy/helm/xp-clean), published to GHCR as oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xp-clean: CronJob run --once into namespace xp-clean; optional manager Deployment off by default

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text: CleanupPolicy CRD + controller-runtime manager, Prometheus exporters, RBAC generator, kubectl plugin alias, multi-cluster, Slack sink implementation, audit retention sinks, SPDX licence packaging.

docs.title: Runtime diagram
docs.text:
How the CLI, cleanup.Runner, policy loader, Kubernetes API, Crossplane XR/MR tree, and Teams notify sink relate at runtime.

Operator → Cobra CLI → cleanup.Runner → discover / match / trace → plan / execute; ConfigMap policy; Kubernetes API + XR/MR tree; AroundRun → Teams Workflows; stdout audit. Open standalone HTML.

docs.title: Teams sequence
docs.text:
Sequence for run --once (default dry-run plan): ConfigMap load, Teams started POST, RunOnce discover/trace, dry-run-delete audit (no Delete), Teams finished POST.

Planner dry-run with Microsoft Teams Workflows webhook POSTs around the run. Open standalone HTML.

Sink configuration and failure isolation: Notifications.

docs.title: Cleanup workflow
docs.text:
One run --once pass: load policy → discover → roots (or opt-in full traces) → plan → execute only with --apply and policy dryRun: false (foreground Delete; optional --wait) → audit → notify finished, with AroundRun started wrap.

End-to-end cleanup pass for a single invocation. Open standalone HTML.

Operational safety gates for this flow are documented under Cleanup.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: How Xp-clean decides what is in scope and how operators express that as policy.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: Topic Why it matters Policy and eligibility ConfigMap discovery, selectors (labels / globs / TTL), deletion scope, and the policy document shape

docs.title: Mental model
docs.text:
1. Policy lives in labelled ConfigMaps (or a file via --config) — not in a CleanupPolicy CRD yet.
  2. Eligibility is labels and/or globs, never “everything in this namespace”.
  3. Deletion scope defaults to the safer instances-only path; definitions need an explicit all scope plus XRD flags.
  4. Dry-run is the default until both policy and CLI ask for live deletes.

For day-to-day run safety, budgets, and Teams hooks, continue in Operations. For command flags, see CLI.

docs.title: Policy and eligibility
docs.text: In-cluster policy uses ConfigMaps in the dedicated xp-clean namespace. A future CleanupPolicy CRD may add richer status UX — ConfigMaps remain the primary surface and are not demoted.

docs.title: ConfigMap discovery
docs.text:
Requirement Value Namespace Dedicated xp-clean by default (--policy-namespace / XP_CLEAN_POLICY_NAMESPACE) Label xp-clean.io/policy=true Data key policy.yaml

Multiple labelled ConfigMaps may coexist for per-team multi-tenancy (different TTLs / selectors per team).

Samples in the repository:

  • config/samples/configmap.yaml — day-1 team A (labels + TTL + roots)
  • config/samples/cleanuppolicy.yaml — file form for --config only
  • config/samples/configmap-team-b.yaml — advanced multi-tenant globs

docs.title: File override
docs.text: Pass --config PATH (or XP_CLEAN_CONFIG) for local or mounted file use. There is no implicit repo-relative sample path.

docs.title: Day-1 essentials
docs.text:
Start with these knobs:

Concern What to set Eligibility selectors.requireLabels (for example xp-clean.io/eligible: "true") TTL ttl.respectResourceTTL + ttl.defaultTTL Dry-run dryRun: true until you are ready; live also needs CLI --apply Mode deletion.mode: roots (default) — highest-parent XRs only Scope deletion.scope: instances-only (default; safer) 
name: team-a
dryRun: true
selectors:
  requireLabels:
    xp-clean.io/eligible: "true"
ttl:
  respectResourceTTL: true
  defaultTTL: 168h
deletion:
  mode: roots
  scope: instances-only

Namespace alone is not enough

Namespace-implies-eligibility is not the model. Eligibility never comes from -n / --namespace on run or plan (that flag is rejected there). Use policy labels and/or globs only. -n is valid on debug trace only.

TTL fields gate when an eligible stack is old enough to delete.

docs.title: Cleanup modes
docs.text: deletion.mode / --mode Behaviour roots (default) Discover + match + highest parents. An XR is a root only if it has no controller ownerReference whose GroupKind is an XR kind (from the cluster XRD set), even when that parent XR was filtered out by selectors / keep / TTL / paused. Dry-run lists those stacks. Live deletes the root XR (foreground propagation); Crossplane GC cleans dependents. No full composition tree walk trace Opt-in. Builds parent→child traces for detailed plans, nested keep/paused gates, orphans, and richer execute

docs.title: Delete semantics
docs.text:
• Live deletes always use Kubernetes DeletionPropagation=Foreground.
  • Waiting after delete is opt-in: deletion.wait: true or CLI --wait. When wait is on, honour deletion.waitTimeout and audit stuck finalizers. When wait is off (default), issue the foreground Delete and continue.
  • Xp-clean never strips Crossplane finalizers.

docs.title: Deletion scope
docs.text: deletion.scope Behaviour instances-only (default) Safer — root XRs (and composed resources via GC / foreground) all Advanced — instances first, then definitions (see below)

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: Still supported in the schema; keep them out of first-run samples unless you need them.

docs.title: Full glob AND matrix
docs.text:
Matching uses labels and/or glob patterns. When both are set, an object must satisfy all non-empty constraint groups (AND).

Mechanism Examples Labels requireLabels: { xp-clean.io/eligible: "true" } Namespace globs team-*-dev, xp-test-* XRD / XR name globs *.dev.example.org, test-* GVK globs group/version patterns (kind not required), e.g. *.dev.example.org/* Deny list namespaceDeny: [kube-system, crossplane-system]

Day-1 ConfigMap samples stay label-only (no globs.gvks). To inject GVK globs without editing the policy document, pass repeatable CLI --gvk-glob on run / plan / manager. When the flag is set it replaces selectors.globs.gvks entirely; when omitted, the policy value (including none) is used. See CLI.

docs.title: mode: trace and scope: all
docs.text: Prefer deletion.mode: trace when you need nested keep/paused visibility, orphan reporting detail, or definition-layer planning. deletion.scope: all deletes instances first, then definitions (CompositionRevision → Composition → XRD) that have zero remaining instances and match selectors. XRD also needs allowXRDDeletion: true.

docs.title: Orphan modes, budgets, wait, notify sinks
docs.text:
Field Notes deletion.wait Opt-in poll-until-gone (default false); override with --wait deletion.waitTimeout Used only when wait is on (default 30m) deletion.orphanMode MVP report surfaces orphans without inventing parallel ownership deletion.maxTracesPerRun / maxDeletesPerRun Per-run budgets deletion.deletePaused Default false — skip crossplane.io/paused ttl.applyDefaultTTLIfMissing Apply defaultTTL when the resource has no TTL annotation observability.notifications Multi-sink schema (Teams MVP); see Notifications schedule / timezone Used by manager interval stub / future cron

Example shape with advanced fields filled in:

name: team-a
schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
dryRun: true
timezone: Europe/London
selectors:
  requireLabels:
    xp-clean.io/eligible: "true"
  globs:
    namespaces: ["team-a-*", "xp-test-*"]
    xrdNames: ["*.dev.example.org"]
    xrNames: ["test-*"]
    gvks: ["*.dev.example.org/*"]   # group/version; kind not required
  namespaceDeny: ["kube-system", "crossplane-system"]
ttl:
  respectResourceTTL: true
  defaultTTL: 168h
  applyDefaultTTLIfMissing: false
deletion:
  mode: trace                       # or roots (default)
  scope: instances-only             # or all
  wait: false
  waitTimeout: 30m
  maxTracesPerRun: 20
  maxDeletesPerRun: 100
  orphanMode: report
  deletePaused: false
  allowXRDDeletion: false
observability:
  verbosity: normal
  notifications:
    enabled: false
    # … see Operations → Notifications

Audit events are JSON lines on stdout when run is verbose (-v / --log-level) or under manager; quiet run prints a human summary only. No audit ConfigMap or object-storage retention sink for now.

docs.title: RBAC note
docs.text:
Lab / backend installs may use broad reader/deleter ClusterRoles for now; tighten later. Prefer installing into the dedicated xp-clean namespace (Helm default).

Next: Cleanup operations for safety gates and the run flow, or Architecture for diagrams of how the runner is wired.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Day-to-day running of Xp-clean: safe cleanup behaviour and optional chat notifications.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
Page Contents Cleanup Safety gates, keep/paused labels, budgets, run flow Notifications Teams Workflows hooks, policy snippet, failure isolation

Install binaries and images under Install. Policy shape and eligibility live under Concepts.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text: How a planned run stays safe once eligibility has selected stacks. Matching rules themselves are covered in Policy and eligibility.

docs.title: Safety gates
docs.text:
• Dry-run by default — run --once always plans first; live deletes need policy dryRun: false and --apply (compatibility: --dry-run=false).
  • Roots by default — deletion.mode: roots plans highest-parent XRs only; opt in to full trees with mode: trace / --mode=trace.
  • Foreground deletes — live Deletes always use DeletionPropagation=Foreground.
  • Wait is opt-in — default is no poll; --wait / deletion.wait: true honours waitTimeout and stuck-finalizer audit.
  • Paused resources — skipped by default (crossplane.io/paused) unless deletePaused: true.
  • Keep label — xp-clean.io/keep=true skips the whole stack.
  • Budgets — advanced: maxTracesPerRun / maxDeletesPerRun.
  • Finalizers — Xp-clean never strips Crossplane finalizers; cloud objects are deleted by Crossplane’s own controllers.
  • Claims / LegacyCluster — out of scope; XR-only / v2-native path.
  • Orphans — advanced: orphanMode: report (MVP) surfaces orphans without inventing parallel ownership.

docs.title: Run flow (summary)
docs.text:
discover XRDs / XRs
  → match labels/globs + TTL
  → highest parents (roots mode) OR build full traces (trace mode)
  → plan deletions (scope + gates)
  → execute only with --apply and policy dryRun: false
       (foreground Delete; optional --wait poll)
  → compact human summary on stdout; audit JSON with `-v` / manager (+ optional Teams notify)

Visual walkthrough: Cleanup workflow.

docs.title: Exit behaviour
docs.text: Use --fail-on-blocked when blocked plans should fail the Job (exit 3). Other exit codes are listed in CLI.

docs.title: Testing cleanup safely
docs.text:
• make test runs unit tests (including pkg/discover) and the in-memory e2e pipeline under test/e2e (dry-run, instances-only delete, keep/paused, exit 3).
  • make e2e runs the same scenarios against kind + Crossplane with XR→ConfigMap/Deployment fixtures (no cloud providers). Local-first — see the repository test/e2e/README.md.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Chat summaries sit beside the CLI summary / audit JSON (when enabled) and metrics. They wrap each RunOnce (started / finished / failed), use a short HTTP deadline, and never change cleanup results or exit codes.

MVP sink: Microsoft Teams Workflows. Slack shares the multi-sink schema but is not implemented yet.

docs.title: Decisions (locked)
docs.text:
• Notify on run start when notifications are enabled (started in notifyOn).
  • Multi-sink schema from day one; Teams first.
  • onDryRun: true — dry-run runs still notify when enabled.
  • Optional logURLTemplate for log deep-links ({{runId}} substituted).
  • SSRF host allow-list is guidance-only for MVP (https-only client; no redirect following).
  • Ships with ConfigMap / --config now — do not wait for a CleanupPolicy CRD.

docs.title: Teams Workflow setup
docs.text:
1. In Teams, create a Workflow owned by the platform team or a channel owner (both are valid; prefer co-owners).
  2. Trigger: When a Teams webhook request is received.
  3. Action: Post card in a chat or channel.
  4. Copy the Workflow callback URL into a Kubernetes Secret (or local env) as XP_CLEAN_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL.
  5. Never commit the URL to git or put it in the ConfigMap policy body.

docs.title: Policy snippet
docs.text:
observability:
  notifications:
    enabled: true
    notifyOn: [started, finished, failed]
    onDryRun: true
    sinks:
      - type: teams
        webhookURLFromEnv: XP_CLEAN_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL
        logURLTemplate: "https://logs.example/search?q={{runId}}"  # optional

Mount the Secret as an env var on the Job / CronJob / Deployment. Overrides:

Flag / env Effect --notify / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY Override notifications.enabled --notify-on-dry-run / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY_ON_DRY_RUN Override onDryRun

docs.title: Teams card content
docs.text:
Finished and dry-run finished cards keep the FactSet counts and add an object list:

Kind Heading Rows Finished (live) Deleted Successfully deleted objects + planner reason Finished (dry-run) Would delete Planned delete steps + planner reason Failed Planned / attempted Plan steps (or audit delete lines) + reason when available Started — Lean card; no object list

Each row is Kind namespace/name — reason (cluster-scoped objects omit the namespace). Reasons are copied from the planner / audit and answer why the object was eligible — for example instance_root; label:xp-clean.io/eligible=true+ttl_elapsed, instance_root; globs+expires-at, or instance_root; label:…+default_ttl. The notify layer does not invent eligibility policy.

Teams finished/failed cards use a full-bleed coloured banner header so the status pops in the channel feed: finished = green (good), failed = red (attention), started = blue (accent). Object lines sit in a nested emphasis block.

Truncation: at most 15 objects are included on the Event / card (notify.MaxObjectsInEvent) to stay under Teams Adaptive Card payload limits. When more targets exist, the card appends … and N more (see Open logs). Full per-object detail remains in the run summary or stdout audit JSON (-v / manager).

Slack sinks share the same Event.Objects fields when implemented; MVP Slack remains unimplemented and counts-oriented.

docs.title: Failure isolation
docs.text:
Each delivery attempt prints a short stderr status (notify started: ok, notify finished: failed: …) and a structured log line. Failures use logr Error (visible under quiet CLI); successes use logr Info (needs -v / manager’s info default) plus the stderr line. Intentional skips (disabled, filtered, or no webhook) stay silent. Notify failures never change cleanup exit codes. Partial multi-sink failure does not fail cleanup. The run summary / audit JSON remains authoritative for what was deleted.
